Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. The application stands disposed of.

3. The petitioners vide the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 seek quashing of FIR No.373/2017 dated 21.12.2017 registered under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 at PS.: Sarita Vihar, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom in view of the Settlement dated 23.02.2019 arrived at between the parties.
This is a digitally signed order.

5.
Petitioner nos.1 to 3 and as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the IO.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.
6. Issue Notice.

sentences.text: 7. Learned APP for the State and learned counsel for the respondent no.2 accept notice.
8. Learned APP for the State confirms that he has no objection to the quashing of the FIR.
9. Respondent no.2 confirms that the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have been granted divorce by mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 24.10.2019.

She further affirms the Settlement dated 23.02.2019 whereby the petitioner no.1 has already paid her a sum of Rs.8,00,000/- and the remaining amount of Rs.4,00,000/- has been handed over to the respondent no.2 vide DD no.894746 dated 27.09.2023 issued on SBI, New Delhi, in full and final settlement of all her claims including alimony, maintenance (present, past and future), stridhan etc.
She states that she has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

10. In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303 and This is a digitally signed order.
